name: Kimi-K3
attention_variant: hybrid: Gated MLA on 24 layers + Kimi Delta Attention on 69 layers, with Attention Residuals
notes: The largest open-weight model in this slice by a wide margin: vendor 2.8T total / 104B activated, safetensors total 2779.93B, native multimodal, 1M context. K3's own card claims 2.5x better scaling efficiency than K2. kv_cache_bytes_per_token = 24 full-attention layers x (kv_lora_rank 512 + qk_rope_head_dim 64) x 2 bytes = 24 x 576 x 2 = 27,648 B/token (27 KiB). This is the clearest illustration of the hybrid-attention trick: 2.78T total parameters with 104B active, yet KV per token is LOWER than Qwen3-8B's 144 KiB (a dense 8B) and less than half of DeepSeek-V3's 68.6 KiB. At 128k context a sequence is 3.38 GiB. Attention composition per the card: 69 KDA + 24 Gated MLA across 93 layers; config linear_attn_config confirms 24 full_attn_layers and 69 kda_layers, with a gate_lower_bound of -5.0 on the KDA layers and a 'Stable LatentMoE' activating 16 of 896 experts. New ingredients versus K2: Attention Residuals, 16 experts per token (up from 8), 896 experts total, and MXFP4 weights with MXFP8 activations from quantization-aware training onward - so the published repo is ALREADY 4-bit, and this is the main practical reason its memory footprint is far below 2.8T would suggest. first_k_dense_replace 1, moe_intermediate_size 3072, intermediate 33792, hidden 7168. num_experts_per_token 16, and 2 shared experts (num_shared_experts 2) - per-token active is 16 routed PLUS 2 always-on shared, worth remembering when reading the vendor's 104B figure.
